title: A Qualitative Study of Physicians' Needs and Barriers in the Counseling of Patients with Familial and Hereditary Prostate Cancer in the German-speaking region
summary:
The aim of this study is to explore physicians' perspectives on the current care of men with familial or hereditary prostate cancer in Germany. Semi-structured interviews will be conducted to identify barriers to the establishment and implementation of specialized counseling services, as well as factors that may facilitate their development and delivery.

The study will include both hospital-based physicians and office-based physicians to capture experiences from different healthcare settings and to identify setting-specific challenges and differences in care.

Based on the findings, practical recommendations will be developed to improve counseling and preventive care for men with familial or hereditary prostate cancer in both outpatient and inpatient settings.

interventions.name: Office-based general practitioners and urologists meeting the following inclusion criteria: completed specialist training and currently practicing as a general practitioner or urologist in Germany; experience in the care of at least 10 patients with prostate cancer per year; working either in privat

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Office-based general practitioners and urologists: Completed specialist training and licensed to practice as office-based physicians in Germany; experience in the care of patients with prostate cancer, corresponding to at least 10 patients per year; working either in private practice or as employed physicians providing statutory health insurance care; ability to provide informed consent.

- Hospital-based urologists: At least in the second year of specialist training in urology; experience in the care of patients with prostate cancer, corresponding to at least 20 patients per year; ability to provide informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
Non-fulfillment of the inclusion criteria; lack of willingness to participate in the interview.
